content: 1. The study by Singal AG, Llovet JM, Yarchoan M, Mehta N, Heimbach JK, Dawson LA, et al., titled AASLD Practice Guidance on Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma, was published in Hepatology in 2023 (Volume 78, Pages 1922–65). 2. McMahon BJ, Bulkow L, Harpster A, Snowball M, Lanier A, Sacco F, et al., conducted a 16-year population-based study on screening for hepatocellular carcinoma in Alaska Natives infected with chronic hepatitis B. The findings were published in Hepatology in 2000 (Volume 32, Issue 4, Part 1, Pages 842–6). 3. Kansagara D, Papak J, Pasha AS, O’Neil M, Freeman M, Relevo R, et al., performed a systematic review on screening for hepatocellular carcinoma in chronic liver disease. The results were published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2014 (Volume 161, Pages 261–9). 4. Tong MJ, Blatt LM, Kao VW, et al., explored surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with chronic viral hepatitis in the United States. Their findings were published in the Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2010 (Volume 16, Pages 553–9). 5. Yu EW, Chie WC, Chen TH, investigated whether screening or surveillance for primary hepatocellular carcinoma using ultrasonography improves patient prognosis. The study was published in Cancer Journal in 2004 (Volume 10, Pages 317–25). 6. Gounder PB compared the cost of screening for hepatocellular carcinoma in individuals with chronic hepatitis B virus infection using ultrasound alone versus a two-step approach involving alpha-fetoprotein followed by ultrasound. The study was published in Hepatology in 2013 (Volume 58, Supplement 1, Pages 388A–9A). 7. Romero MA conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of a clinical pathway for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance in Colombia. The findings were published in Value in Health in 2010 (Volume 13, Page A40). 8. Coon JTR reviewed the surveillance of cirrhosis for hepatocellular carcinoma, including a systematic review and economic analysis. The study was published in Health Technology Assessment in 2007 (Volume 11, Pages 1–206). 9. Aghoram R, Cai P, Dickinson JA, evaluated the use of alpha-fetoprotein and/or liver ultrasonography for screening hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with chronic hepatitis B. The findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2012 (CD002799). 10. Singal AG, Lampertico P, Nahon P, discussed new trends in the epidemiology and surveillance of hepatocellular carcinoma. The study was published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2020 (Volume 72, Pages 250–61). 11. Costentin CE, Layese R, Bourcier V, Cagnot C, Marcellin P, Guyader D, et al., demonstrated that compliance with hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance guidelines is associated with increased lead-time adjusted survival in patients with compensated viral cirrhosis. The study was published in Gastroenterology. 12. Chen CJ, Yang HI, Su J, Jen CL, You SL, Lu SN, et al., examined the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma across a biological gradient of serum hepatitis B virus DNA levels. The study was published in JAMA in 2006 (Volume 295, Pages 65–73). 13. Yuen MF, Yuan HJ, Wong DK, Yuen JC, Wong WM, Chan AO, et al., identified prognostic determinants for chronic hepatitis B in Asians and discussed therapeutic implications. The study was published in Gut in 2005 (Volume 54, Pages 1610–4). 14. Ribes J, Clèries R, Rubio A, Hernández JM, Mazzara R, Madoz P, et al., investigated cofactors associated with liver disease mortality in an HBsAg-positive Mediterranean cohort over 20 years of follow-up. The study was published in the International Journal of Cancer in 2006 (Volume 119, Pages 687–94). 15. Seo SI, Choi HS, Choi BY, Kim HS, Kim HY, Jang MK, et al., found that the coexistence of hepatitis B surface antigen and antibody to hepatitis B surface may increase the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma in chronic hepatitis B virus infection. The study was published in the Journal of Medical Virology in 2014 (Volume 86, Pages 124–30). 16. Hann HW, Fu X, Myers RE, Hann RS, Wan S, Kim SH, et al., evaluated the predictive value of alpha-fetoprotein in the long-term risk of developing hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with hepatitis B virus infection. The study was published in the European Journal of Cancer in 2012 (Volume 48, Pages 2319–27). 17. Yang R, Gui X, Xiong Y, Gao S, Zhang Y, Deng L, et al., assessed the risk of liver-associated morbidity and mortality in a cohort of HIV and HBV co-infected Han Chinese. The study was published in Infection in 2011 (Volume 39, Pages 427–31). 18. Shimakawa Y, Yan HJ, Tsuchiya N, Bottomley C, Hall AJ, reviewed the association of early age at establishment of chronic hepatitis B infection with persistent viral replication, liver cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The study was published in PLoS One in 2013 (Volume 8, e69430). 19. Kramvis A discussed the molecular characteristics and clinical relevance of African genotypes and subgenotypes of hepatitis B virus. The study was published in the South African Medical Journal in 2018 (Volume 108, Supplement 1, Pages S17–S21). 20. McMahon BJ, Nolen LD, Snowball M, Homan C, Negus S, Roik E, et al., identified HBV genotype as a significant risk factor in determining which patients with chronic HBV infection should undergo surveillance for HCC. The study was published in Hepatology in 2021 (Volume 74, Pages 2965–73).
